title: HB175 (2021 Regular): Public Safety - Ammunition - Sales and Transfers

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2021RS/bills/hb/hb0175f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader as filed; no vote on record. § 5-704(a) lists the record fields (date, ID number, brand, type and amount, name, address, birth date, phone, salesperson); § 5-702 exempts sales to licensed dealers, handgun qualification licence holders, gunsmiths, officers and others. Neither is quoted for length.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-703(a)): BEFORE THE SALE OR TRANSFER OF AMMUNITION, AN AMMUNITION VENDOR SHALL: (1) CONFIRM IDENTIFICATION OF THE PURCHASER OR TRANSFEREE THROUGH THE PRESENTATION OF A DRIVER’S LICENSE OR OTHER GOVERNMENT–ISSUED IDENTIFICATION; AND (2) CONDUCT A BACKGROUND CHECK ON THE PURCHASER OR TRANSFEREE THROUGH THE NICS INDEX.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-703(b)): IF THE RESULTS OF THE NICS INDEX BACKGROUND CHECK INDICATE THAT THE PURCHASER OR TRANSFEREE IS PROHIBITED FROM POSSESSING A FIREARM UNDER FEDERAL LAW, THE AMMUNITION VENDOR MAY NOT COMPLETE THE SALE OR TRANSFER.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-704(c)(1)): AN AMMUNITION VENDOR SHALL ELECTRONICALLY SUBMIT TO THE SECRETARY THE INFORMATION REQUIRED UNDER SUBSECTION (A) OF THIS SECTION FOR ALL SALES AND TRANSFERS OF AMMUNITION.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-704(c)(2)): THE SECRETARY SHALL RETAIN THE INFORMATION IN AN ELECTRONIC DATABASE THAT REMAINS CONFIDENTIAL AND MAY BE USED ONLY FOR LAW ENFORCEMENT PURPOSES.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-705(a)): A PERSON THAT VIOLATES THIS SUBTITLE IS GUILTY OF A CIVIL OFFENSE AND ON CONVICTION SHALL BE FINED NOT LESS THAN $1,000 FOR EACH VIOLATION.
